title: K-th Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix

constraints: All the rows and columns of matrix are guaranteed to be sorted in non-decreasing order.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: The elements in the matrix are [1,5,9,10,11,12,13,13,15], and the 8^th smallest number is 13

content.problemStatement:
With an `n x n` `matrix` where each of the rows and columns is sorted in ascending order, output *the* `k^th` *smallest element in the matrix*.

Keep in mind that it is the `k^th` smallest element **in the sorted order**, not the `k^th` **distinct** element.

You must find a solution with a memory complexity better than `O(n^2)`.

**Example 1:**

```
Input: matrix = [[1,5,9],[10,11,13],[12,13,15]], k = 8
Output: 13
Explanation: The elements in the matrix are [1,5,9,10,11,12,13,13,15], and the 8^th smallest number is 13
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: matrix = [[-5]], k = 1
Output: -5
```

**Constraints:**

* `n == matrix.length == matrix[i].length`
* `1 <= n <= 300`
* `-10^9 <= matrix[i][j] <= 10^10`
* All the rows and columns of `matrix` are **guaranteed** to be sorted in **non-decreasing order**.
* `1 <= k <= n^2`

**Follow up:**

* Could you solve the problem with a constant memory (i.e., `O(1)` memory complexity)?
* Could you solve the problem in `O(n)` time complexity? The solution may be too advanced for an interview but you may find reading [this paper](http://www.cse.yorku.ca/~andy/pubs/X+Y.pdf) fun.

notes: At most one frontier entry per row is kept in the heap.
The kth extracted value is the kth smallest matrix element.
solution.approach: Use a min-heap containing the smallest unprocessed value from each row. Pop the minimum k times; after removing (r,c), push (r,c+1) when it exists. Because each row is sorted, the heap represents the frontier of all remaining candidates.

better.complexity: O(k log n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.
better.description: Merge the n sorted rows with a min-heap initialized from the first element of every row. Each extraction advances one row by one position.

optimal.complexity: O(k log n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.
optimal.description: Maintain one candidate from each row in a min-heap. Extract the smallest candidate and insert the next value from the same row until k values have been extracted.

bruteForce.complexity: O(n^2 log(n^2)) time and O(n^2) space.
bruteForce.description: Flatten all n^2 elements, sort them, and return the element at index k-1.

code.C++: class Solution{public:long long kthSmallest(vector<vector<long long>>&m,int k){using T=tuple<long long,int,int>;priority_queue<T,vector<T>,greater<T>>q;for(int r=0;r<(int)m.size();r++)q.emplace(m[r][0],r,0);long long ans=0;for(int i=0;i<k;i++){auto[v,r,c]=q.top();q.pop();ans=v;if(c+1<(int)m.size())q.emplace(m[r][c+1],r,c+1);}return ans;}};

followUps: Can you solve it with O(1) extra space using binary search on the value range?
How would the method change for a rectangular matrix?
Why is one heap entry per row sufficient?
